supporting_observations.claim: The PowerShell process was recorded at 13:45:02 UTC, several minutes after the reported approximate time, and ran as ken.ito on WS-MSANTOS-01.
Shortly before PowerShell started, WS-MSANTOS-01 recorded a network logon for ken.ito from WS-KITO-01; the logon received special privileges.
PowerShell's command line runs the inventory-listed Patch-Workstations.ps1 script from FILE-BLU-01, matching the organization's stated IT patching practice.
The PowerShell process launched wusa to install a Windows update, and the workstation made a large download.windowsupdate.com transfer during the same patching activity.

The observed process and its surrounding activity are consistent with the scheduled, authorized workstation patching described in the environment context; the evidence does not show a separate PowerShell execution around 13:40.

known_telemetry_limitations: The process-creation records show PowerShell's command line but do not include the contents or integrity of Patch-Workstations.ps1.
The process records establish that PowerShell ran, but do not establish whether its window was visible to the user or how long it was visible.
The recorded PowerShell start is at 13:45:02 UTC, so the evidence cannot establish the exact time of the window Mia reported around 13:40.
claims_not_established: Whether the script or the update package was modified or otherwise compromised.
Whether Mia saw the recorded 13:45 PowerShell execution, or whether a separate, unrecorded PowerShell window appeared around 13:40.
additional_evidence_needed: If confirming the reported timing is operationally necessary, obtain Mia's more precise recollection or endpoint UI/process telemetry for the reported time.
For independent validation of the patch run, review the script and update package contents, hashes, and corresponding IT patch records.
